questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Glad hands can be connected to any other glad hands.
Only connect one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is typically used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, where should cargo be placed?

options.text: As high as possible inside the trailer.
As low as possible inside the trailer.
On the driver's side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible inside the trailer.
questions.explanation: Vehicles that are top-heavy are more likely to roll over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible in the trailer to reduce this risk.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer straight, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.
Back toward the driver's side.
Back toward the passenger's side.

questions.explanation: If you cannot back straight, use a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: When testing ____, apply your brakes with the hand control while moving forward slowly.

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System
The emergency braking system
The trailer service brakes

questions.explanation: To test trailer service brakes, first check that air pressure is normal, then release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and use the hand control to apply brakes. If working properly, you will feel the brakes activate.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be directly behind the cab?

options.text: The lightest
The heaviest
The smallest

questions.explanation: Place the heaviest-loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer at the rear.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, how should cargo be loaded?

options.text: With most weight on the driver's side.
Near the rear of the trailer.
Spread evenly throughout the trailer.

questions.explanation: Distribute cargo weight evenly in the trailer to reduce rollover risk. Do not place too much weight on one side.

questions.question: When coupling, what should you do?

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands.
Connect only one set of glad hands.
Leave one glad hand loose.

questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are sometimes color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is typically used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: About five inches
A maximum of two inches
No space

questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Makes sure the engine has enough oil.
Stops the tractor from going too fast.
Keeps air in the truck brakes if the trailer leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the truck brakes if the trailer leaks.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. The valve closes automatically if air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: How do fully-loaded rigs compare to empty rigs in terms of rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They have the same chance of rolling over.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs roll over more easily than empty rigs. The heavy cargo raises the center of gravity, making the vehicle more unstable.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It lets the wheels lock up.
It stops the wheels from locking up.
It makes turning easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS helps stop the wheels from locking during hard braking. When ABS detects a wheel about to lock, it reduces brake pressure to keep the wheel turning.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
The vehicle will stop too quickly.
It can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause the trailer to skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: What do you test by placing the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position?

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes.
A coupling device.
The anti-lock brakes.

questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. Pull out the trailer air supply control or move it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: Are combination vehicles easier or harder to drive than single commercial vehicles?

options.text: Easier to drive.
Lighter in weight.
More difficult to drive.

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving while pulling trailers?

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Press the accelerator all the way down when starting.

questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, where should the tractor be positioned?

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.
Directly next to the trailer.
Parallel with the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle can move the trailer and break the landing gear.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
Prevents a truck from being stolen.
Prevents a trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. The valve closes automatically if air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, what is the minimum following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, keep at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.
